newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Falklanders angered over Argentine music incident.
newsitem.headline: Falklanders angered over Argentine music incident.

text.p: Falkland Islanders reacted angrily on Wednesday to news that an Argentine band had played a march calling for sovereignty over the islands in front of British soldiers competing in a skiing competition in Argentina.
The squad of British troops marched to the tune before Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez in the southern Andean resort of Bariloche.
Argentine Army chief General Martin Balza praised the British team for respecting their hosts' musical tastes.

"It was a display of exceptional bad manners by General Balza and probably close to an insult to those British soldiers and officials attending," said Michael Summers, a councillor on the fervently pro-British Falkland Islands.
Councillor Sharon Halford called the Argentine action "extremely bad taste but unfortunately it was what you might expect from the Argentine military. It is their mentality".

Argentina has disputed the sovereignty of the islands it calls the Malvinas with Britain for more than 160 years. In 1982 its then ruling military junta sent a force to snatch control of the South Atlantic archipelago.
Britain then won a 10-week war in which about 1,000 troops, mainly Argentines, were killed.
